title: Account Management Standard for Larkspur Credit Cards: Suspension, Closure, Charge-Off and Limit Changes
content:
This standard governs when an account on the Larkspur Credit Cards is suspended, reinstated, closed or charged off, and when its credit limit may change.

## 1. Suspension and reinstatement

Charging privileges are suspended at the card's suspension threshold of days past due, or during a fraud review. They are restored once the amount past due is 0.00 and any review is cleared.

## 2. Closure

- **By the cardholder.** A cardholder may close the account at any time. The balance is still repaid under the account terms, and unredeemed rewards are forfeited.
- **For inactivity.** Larkspur may close an account with a 0.00 balance after the card's inactivity period, in months, without transactions.

## 3. Charge-off

An account is charged off once the current date is at least the charge-off days past due after the oldest unpaid due date. Days past due are counted in calendar days starting the day after the oldest unpaid due date.

The terms of this test are:

| Element | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Starting point | The oldest unpaid due date, as shown on the account record as its payment due date |
| Unit | Calendar days. The day after the oldest unpaid due date is day 1 past due |
| Length | The card's charge-off threshold, in days past due |
| Comparison | Not earlier than. The account is charged off on the day the count reaches the threshold, and on any later day |
| Source of the dates | The system record of that same account, read as of today |

**Days past due on an account.** These are the calendar days from the payment due date shown on the account to today. This applies when an amount past due above 0.00 is shown and that due date is earlier than today. Otherwise the account is 0 days past due.

## 4. Credit limit changes

- **Increase.** A limit increase is considered no sooner than the card's minimum number of months after opening, or after the last increase. It is never above the card's maximum limit.
- **Decrease.** A decrease requested by the cardholder takes effect at once. It never goes below the balance or the card's minimum limit.

The thresholds and limits named above are the figures in the card's product terms.

## Boundary cases on an invented threshold

To keep the arithmetic visible, these cases assume a hypothetical charge-off threshold of 10 days past due. That is not the card's figure. The oldest unpaid due date is the 1st of a month, and the amount stays unpaid.

| Date | Days past due | Charged off? |
|---|---|---|
| the 1st (the due date itself) | 0 | No |
| the 2nd | 1 | No |
| the 10th | 9 | No, because this is the day before the boundary |
| the 11th | 10 | Yes, because this is the boundary day and equality satisfies "at least" |
| the 12th | 11 | Yes |

## Hypothetical limit decrease

The figures are invented. A card has a minimum limit of 500.00 and a balance of 800.00, and the cardholder asks to lower the limit to 600.00. The new limit may go no lower than the higher of the balance and the minimum limit. Here that floor is 800.00, so a limit of 600.00 is not available. A limit of 900.00 would take effect at once.
